setup: Set a cable pulley to mid-chest height and attach a single D-handle.
Grasp the handle with a neutral grip and step away from the machine, turning your body roughly 30 to 45 degrees away from the cable column so the line of pull matches your pectoral fibers.
Adopt a stable staggered stance with the opposite-side foot forward, holding the machine frame with the non-working hand if needed for additional stability.
steps: Begin with your elbow bent and tucked slightly, allowing the cable to pull your arm back into a comfortable chest stretch.
Press the handle forward and diagonally across your torso past your sternal midline while extending your elbow.
Squeeze your pectoral fully in the peak contracted position across the body without twisting your torso.
Reverse the motion under control, returning your arm until a deep pectoral stretch is achieved before initiating the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you allow the weight to pull into the stretch; exhale as you press across your chest.
cues: Wrap your bicep across your sternum
Stay braced and resist twisting through your hips
Drive across the midline, not just forward

common_faults.fault: Rotating the entire torso toward the pressing side during the press.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core and maintain a fixed torso angle so the chest muscles perform the adduction rather than spine rotation.
Ensure the working hand crosses past the center of your chest to achieve a full shortened contraction of the pectoralis major.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the working shoulder upward toward the ear.
common_faults.correction: Keep the scapula depressed and stable against your ribcage throughout the movement.

precautions: Avoid letting the cable excessively hyperextend the shoulder joint at the deep stretch position.

name: Single-Arm Cable Press-Around
summary: A unilateral cable chest press performed across the midline to train the pectoralis major through an extended horizontal adduction range of motion.
